interest: Illuminates Japan's wartime textile regulations, shift toward Brazilian cotton, and transfer of spinning machinery to the occupied Philippines.
overview: This file comprises U.S. State Department records from August 1940 to January 1943 concerning Japan's cotton textile industry during World War II. It features an extensive voluntary report from the American Consulate at Osaka reviewing the 1939–1940 season, analyzing production curtailment, mounting piece goods surpluses, link system controls, and a shift toward Brazilian raw cotton imports with detailed statistical tables. Additionally, it contains a 1943 despatch from the U.S. Embassy in Buenos Aires transmitting Japanese press reports on the wartime reorganization of the spinning industry under a block system and the planned transfer of surplus spinning equipment to the occupied Philippines.
